title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.91 and context): each set E carries a closure structure. Σ_E is the family of 'supports' in E. Sup°_E(A), written supp°_E(A) on this page, is the smallest support containing A. There is also an incidence or orthogonality relation x |o| y, with 'cosupports' such as cosupp°{x'} (apparently the orthogonal of x', which is a support). A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces ᾱ : P(E) → P(E'), the image ∪_{x∈A} α(x). It also induces α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'}, given by α_*(S) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)).

The proposition of p.91 lists equivalent conditions on α:
(i) α has a transpose β : E' → P(E), with x |o| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |o| x'.
(ii) α_*(supp°_E A) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)) for all A; that is, A and its support hull have images with the same support hull.
(iii) For every support S' of E', the 'inverse image' {x | α(x) ⊂ S'} is a support of E.
(iv) For every x', the set β(x') = {x | α(x) |o| x'} is in Σ_E.
(v) a) α_* commutes with arbitrary Sups; b) α_*(supp° x) = supp°(α(x)).

This page proves the cycle (i)⇒(ii)⇒(iii)⇒(iv)⇒(i), then that these imply (v).
- (ii)⇒(iii): put S = {x | α(x) ⊂ S'} and S̄ = supp°_E S ⊇ S. Then ᾱ(S) ⊂ S', and S' is a support. By (ii), supp ᾱ(S̄) = supp ᾱ(S) ⊂ S', so ᾱ(S̄) ⊂ S'. Hence S̄ ⊂ S, so S = S̄ ∈ Σ_E.
- (iii)⇒(iv): take S' = cosupp°{x'}.
- (iv)⇒(i): define the transpose through complements, β(x') = ∁γ(x'). The adjunction x |o| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |o| x' is then just the definition of γ.
- (i)–(iv)⇒(v)a): for a family S_i in Σ_E, Sup S_i = supp°(∪S_i). So α_*(Sup S_i) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(∪S_i)) = supp°_{E'}(∪ᾱ(S_i)), and p.93 finishes this as Sup_i α_*(S_i).

Purpose: build a category of 'closure/orthogonality spaces' whose morphisms are correspondences with transposes. These are identified with join-preserving maps Σ → Σ' between the complete lattices of supports (the 'Scholie' on p.93: Corr(Σ,Σ') ≃ Corr(E,E')). This is the standard dictionary between relations admitting adjoints and morphisms of sup-lattices.
errors: (i)⇒(ii) is declared trivial without argument. It needs the fact that, under a transpose, preimages of supports are supports (essentially (iii)). This is easy but not literally immediate.

The equivalences are stated before (v) is properly formulated. Grothendieck notes on p.93 that he had to add condition v b) after the fact to get the converse (v)⇒(ii). So the statement on p.91 was being repaired during the proof.

The handwriting makes it ambiguous whether supports are defined via the orthogonality |o| (bi-orthogonal closure) or abstractly. The step (iii)⇒(iv) silently uses that cosupp°{x'} is a support and that α(x) ⊂ cosupp°{x'} ⇔ ¬(α(x) |o| x') (or the complementary convention).

ideas.what: Lattice Σ_E of 'supports' (closed sets of a closure operator supp°) on a set with an incidence/orthogonality relation; Sup in Σ_E is the closure of the union.
ideas.modern_name: Closure system / Moore family; Galois-closed (bi-orthogonal) sets of an orthogonality space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moore, Birkhoff (1940), Ore (Galois connexions, 1944); orthogonality spaces: Dacey, Foulis–Randall

ideas.what: Equivalence: a correspondence α:E→P(E') has a transpose β with x |o| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |o| x' iff α_* : Σ_E→Σ_E' preserves arbitrary sups iff inverse images of supports are supports.
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint (Galois-adjoint) maps between orthogonality spaces ↔ join-preserving maps of their closed-set lattices; 'continuous' relations between closure spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Order-theoretic adjoint functor theorem (folklore); in orthogonality/property-lattice setting: Foulis–Randall, Moore (1995), Faure–Frölicher

ideas.what: Category whose morphisms are correspondences E→P(E') with transposes, identified with Corr(Σ,Σ') = sup-preserving maps (Scholie on next page).
ideas.modern_name: Category Sup of complete lattices with join-preserving maps; relational/Chu-space presentation of it
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joyal–Tierney (1984) for Sup; Chu construction (Barr); Moore's state-property duality

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but routine order-theoretic proposition: relations with transposes correspond to sup-preserving maps of closure lattices. It is well known in lattice theory and in the orthogonality-space/quantum-logic literature. The page is of mild biographical interest only, showing Grothendieck in 1986 building such a formalism from scratch.
transcription_corrections: Where the transcription reads 'int°_E', the image reads 'supp°_E' (written 's—pp°_E'). This holds for both 'S̄ = supp°_E S ⊃ S' and 'Sup^{Σ_E} S_i = supp°_E(∪S_i)'.
In the final formula the image reads 'α_*(S) = α_*(supp°_E(∪S_i)) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(∪S_i))', with the underbrace ∪ᾱ(S_i).
'(iii) ⇒ (iv) trivial' is better read 'se déduit/trivial, prenant S' = cosupp° {x'}'.
The word before the final formula is 'donc', which was struck through and rewritten.
The interlinear insertion reads approximately 'b) est clair par (ii) et [?] a)' rather than '(i) est clair par (ii) et (iv)'.
The transcription's '(v[?])' is indeed '(v)', the condition from p.91 about commuting with Sups.
